question_text: Five days after undergoing right hemicolectomy for colon cancer, a 62-year-old man has fever, abdominal pain, nausea, and urinary frequency. The surgery was uncomplicated. An indwelling urinary catheter was placed intraoperatively. His temperature is 39.4°C (102.9°F), pulse is 91/min, and blood pressure is 118/83 mm Hg. There is tenderness to palpation of the costovertebral angle. The urine collected in the catheter bag appears cloudy. Which of the following measures is most likely to have prevented this patient's current condition?

                    ### Question
                    Five days after undergoing right hemicolectomy for colon cancer, a 62-year-old man has fever, abdominal pain, nausea, and urinary frequency. The surgery was uncomplicated. An indwelling urinary catheter was placed intraoperatively. His temperature is 39.4°C (102.9°F), pulse is 91/min, and blood pressure is 118/83 mm Hg. There is tenderness to palpation of the costovertebral angle. The urine collected in the catheter bag appears cloudy. Which of the following measures is most likely to have prevented this patient's current condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Urinary antiseptics
opb. Early removal of catheter
opc. Antimicrobial prophylaxis
opd. Periurethral care
ope. Daily catheter replacement

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely measure to have prevented the patient's current condition is early removal of the indwelling urinary catheter. The presence of the catheter increases the risk of urinary tract infection, leading to cloudy urine, fever, abdominal pain, and other symptoms. Early removal of the catheter can help prevent bacterial colonization and subsequent urinary tract infections, ultimately reducing the risk of sepsis.
